name: Close deficiencies and reach substantial performance
summary: When a building is nearly finished, the contractor must find and fix incomplete or defective work, get occupancy approved, have the consultant certify substantial performance and publish the certificate, and hand the building to the owner with manuals, as-builts and training. The superintendent and assistant superintendent run the deficiency walks and trades, the project manager handles the applications, and the commissioning coordinator assembles the turnover package. It is slow because trades have left for other jobs, consultants and inspectors book weeks out, closeout documents must be chased, and the certificate date starts the lien and holdback clock.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 employees building institutional, commercial and industrial buildings, with about 220 active projects run from regional offices, a web-based project management platform and a construction ERP.
baseline.notes: Practice described for Ontario stipulated-price and construction-management projects on CCDC contract forms; Western and Atlantic projects follow the same pattern under their provincial lien and safety laws.

trigger: The superintendent declares the building substantially complete and ready for deficiency review.
end_state: The certificate of substantial performance is published, the owner has taken over the building, and the consultant's deficiency list is closed or carried to warranty.

volume.seasonality: More handovers in July and August (schools before Labour Day) and in December and March (owner fiscal and calendar year-ends).

evidence.note: Equal to new project starts in steady state: 220 active projects over an average 22-month duration (organisation demand driver project-starts).

surge.cause: summer handover rush for schools needed by Labour Day

evidence.note: School boards require occupancy before September; kept from the organisation file.
Share of the role's time on deficiency closeout and handover, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 120 superintendents x 0.05; about two months of part-time effort per handover.
Share of the role's time on deficiency closeout and handover, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 90 assistant superintendents x about 0.07.
Share of the role's time on deficiency closeout and handover, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 110 project managers x about 0.02.

Share of the role's time on deficiency closeout and handover, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 15 coordinators x 0.4; the rest of their time is commissioning and closeout documents.

systems.name: Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Equipment management (fleet register, rates, maintenance work orders)
Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)

resources.name: Telehandlers, skid steers and aerial work platforms
Flatbed and boom trucks for yard deliveries
Site office trailers and sea containers
Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Plan the handover
steps.description: The superintendent reviews the schedule, the open work of each trade, commissioning status and the owner's occupancy date, and sets dates for the internal deficiency walk, the occupancy inspection, the consultant's review and the handover meeting.

error.defect_description: Handover date set before life-safety commissioning can be finished.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from practice.

steps.name: Walk the building and record the contractor's deficiency list
steps.description: The assistant superintendent walks every room, roof and service space with a tablet, records each incomplete or defective item with a photo, location and responsible trade in the project platform, and uses an aerial lift for high ceilings and atria.

error.defect_description: Items in ceiling spaces and rooms not accessed are missed.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 elevating work platform rules and fall protection; operator trained on the platform

evidence.note: A 10,000 to 30,000 square metre institutional building takes several days to walk; 10 to 45 hours of assistant superintendent time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue deficiency lists to the trades
steps.description: The assistant superintendent sorts the list by trade, sends each subcontractor its items through the platform or by email with a completion date, and reviews progress at the weekly subcontractor meeting.

error.defect_description: Items assigned to the wrong trade bounce between trades.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Trades correct the contractor's list
steps.description: Subcontractor crews return to fix paint, ceilings, doors and hardware, trims, mechanical and electrical devices and labelling; trades with crews already moved to other jobs are slow to come back.

error.defect_description: Items are marked complete but not fixed.

evidence.note: One to three weeks for trades to work through the list; author's estimate. Trade labour is outside the organisation and not counted.

steps.name: Confirm life-safety and systems commissioning
steps.description: The commissioning coordinator collects the fire alarm verification, sprinkler and standpipe test, emergency lighting, elevator, backflow and generator certificates and the commissioning reports, and checks nothing needed for occupancy is outstanding.

error.defect_description: A certificate the building department requires is missing at inspection.

control.basis: Ontario Building Code occupancy requirements: fire alarm verification and life-safety systems tested before occupancy

evidence.note: Waits on testing agencies and the commissioning process; author's estimate.

steps.name: Building department and fire inspections for occupancy
steps.description: The municipal building inspector and fire prevention officer inspect the building, review the life-safety certificates and either permit occupancy or list items that must be fixed and re-inspected.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Ontario Building Code Act: occupancy of a new building permitted only after inspection

evidence.note: Booking lead time of a few days to two weeks; failure rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Correct occupancy items and rebook
steps.description: The superintendent gets the trades to fix the items on the inspector's list, such as fire separations, door hardware or signage, collects the missing certificate and rebooks the inspection.

error.defect_description: Fix incomplete; second failure.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request the consultant's substantial performance review
steps.description: The project manager writes to the consultant that the work is ready for review for substantial performance, attaches the status of the contractor's list and the occupancy permit, and proposes dates for the review walk.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Walk the building with the consultant
steps.description: The superintendent accompanies the architect and the mechanical and electrical engineers through the building over one or more days, opening rooms and ceiling access and noting what each consultant records.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Consultants book reviews one to two weeks out; one to three days of walking; author's estimate.

steps.name: Consultant issues its deficiency list
steps.description: The architect and engineers compile their observations into a formal deficiency list with item numbers, which becomes the list the contractor must complete and the basis for valuing incomplete work.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: CCDC 2-2008 GC 5.4.2 ties substantial performance review to a list of items to be completed or corrected (src pawson); timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Log the consultant's list and assign items
steps.description: The superintendent keys or imports the consultant's items into the platform, merges them with the open contractor items, assigns each to a trade with a date, and sends the lists out.

error.defect_description: Items are re-keyed wrongly or duplicated.

evidence.note: Re-keying from the consultant's PDF or spreadsheet was common in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the application for substantial performance
steps.description: The project manager values the incomplete and deficient work, checks the value against the statutory substantial performance threshold, and sends the application with the list of items to be completed, the statutory declaration and the WSIB clearance to the consultant.

error.defect_description: Incomplete work undervalued; application rejected.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act: substantial performance defined by value of work remaining; contract requires application with list of items (CCDC 2 GC 5.4)

evidence.note: Application with list of items (src pawson); substantial performance as defined in lien legislation (src mlt).

steps.name: Consultant verifies and certifies substantial performance
steps.description: The consultant checks the valuation and the list, and as payment certifier signs the certificate of substantial performance with its date, or tells the contractor what must be finished first.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act: payment certifier certifies substantial performance; CCDC 2-2008 GC 5.4.2 20 calendar days

next.condition: not yet; more items to complete

evidence.note: CCDC 2-2008 GC 5.4.2 gives the consultant 20 calendar days after the application and list (src pawson); the mode of 7 days reflects consultants who certify sooner, the high reflects late certification. The 18% not-yet share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Publish the certificate and notify finance
steps.description: The project manager arranges publication of the certificate of substantial performance in a construction trade newspaper, sends the certificate to the subcontractors and to finance, and diarises the end of the 60-day lien period for holdback release.

error.defect_description: Lien period end date diarised wrongly.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act: publication of the certificate of substantial performance starts the 60-day lien preservation period

evidence.note: Publication of the certificate as trigger and 60-day lien preservation period (src dla); publication lead time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assemble the turnover package
steps.description: The commissioning coordinator compiles operations and maintenance manuals, warranties, as-built drawings, spare parts and attic stock lists and test reports from every trade into the owner's required format, and checks them against the specification closeout list.

error.defect_description: Manual missing a trade's warranty or as-built drawing.

evidence.note: Ten to forty hours of compiling per project; author's estimate. Runs in parallel with the consultant's certification in practice.

steps.name: Chase trades for missing closeout documents
steps.description: The commissioning coordinator emails and phones trades for missing manuals, warranties and as-builts, escalates to the project manager, and warns that holdback or final payment will be held until documents arrive.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Chasing trades for closeout documents is a familiar closeout bottleneck; author's estimate.

steps.name: Train the owner's operators
steps.description: The commissioning coordinator schedules and runs training sessions in which trades and equipment suppliers show the owner's facility staff how to operate and maintain systems, and records attendance for the turnover package.

error.defect_description: A system is handed over without training.

evidence.note: Training and O&M documentation are part of Ready-for-Takeover under CCDC 2-2020 (src mlt); timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Apply for Ready-for-Takeover
steps.description: The project manager sends the consultant the application for Ready-for-Takeover with the certificate, occupancy permit, turnover package, as-builts, start-up test results and training records, and requests the takeover date.

error.defect_description: A prerequisite document is missing.

evidence.note: Ready-for-Takeover prerequisites under CCDC 2-2020 GC 12.1 (src mlt).

steps.name: Consultant reviews Ready-for-Takeover
steps.description: The consultant checks the prerequisites and either confirms the takeover date or lists what is missing; on CCDC 2-1994 and 2008 contracts the owner's acceptance of the turnover package plays the same role.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 GC 12.1 Ready-for-Takeover: consultant responds within 10 calendar days

evidence.note: Consultant has 10 calendar days to respond (src mlt); the 15% return share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold the handover meeting
steps.description: The superintendent walks the owner's facility manager through the building, hands over keys, access cards, attic stock and spare parts, transfers site security and utilities, and gets the handover certificate signed.

error.defect_description: Keys or attic stock not recorded; later dispute.

control.basis: Ontario OHSA: constructor responsibility for the site ends and control passes to the owner at handover; utilities and fire protection transferred

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request demobilisation of trailer and equipment
steps.description: The superintendent sends the equipment request to the yard coordinator to remove the site trailer, containers, hoarding and company equipment, and cancels temporary power, water and waste services.

error.defect_description: A rental item is left on site and keeps charging.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Demobilise the site
steps.description: The assistant superintendent supervises loading of the trailer, containers, fencing and small tools onto boom trucks, checks the laydown area is restored, and records what went back to the yard.

error.defect_description: Damage to owner's landscaping during removal.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 lifting and rigging rules for boom truck lifts; company lift plan

evidence.note: Waits for a boom truck from the yard, which is busy with mobilisations; author's estimate.

steps.name: Seasonal exterior items wait for suitable weather
steps.description: Asphalt top coat, line painting, sod and planting and some roofing or sealant items cannot be done in winter, so they are carried on the list with a value held back until spring.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: About a quarter of handovers fall in the October to March period with exterior items deferred; two weeks to five months of waiting; author's estimate.

steps.name: Trades close the consultant's items in the occupied building
steps.description: Trades return to finish the consultant's items while the owner occupies the building, often working evenings or weekends or waiting for the owner to give access to occupied rooms.

error.defect_description: Items reported complete but not fixed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of time to close the consultant's list after occupancy.

steps.name: Drive back to the occupied site
steps.description: With the trailer gone, the assistant superintendent drives from another project or the office to the occupied building for the back-check, signing in with the owner's facility staff.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Back-check closed items with the consultant
steps.description: The assistant superintendent checks every item reported closed, walks the remaining items with the architect, closes them in the platform, and returns any not properly fixed to the trade.

error.defect_description: An item is closed without checking.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Close out and notify warranty and finance
steps.description: The project manager confirms the deficiency list is complete, writes to the consultant and owner, and tells warranty, finance and the closeout team so warranty start dates, holdback release and final billing can proceed.

error.defect_description: Warranty start date recorded wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Failed occupancy inspection
exceptions.description: The building or fire inspector lists items such as fire separations, door hardware or missing certificates; they are fixed and the inspection rebooked.

exceptions.name: Substantial performance not yet certified
exceptions.description: The consultant finds too much work outstanding and the contractor must close more items before re-applying.

exceptions.name: Seasonal exterior items deferred
exceptions.description: Winter handovers carry asphalt, landscaping and similar items until spring.

exceptions.name: Missing closeout documents
exceptions.description: Trades have not delivered manuals, warranties or as-builts, and the coordinator chases them, sometimes after the consultant rejects the takeover application.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from completion notice to deficiency list closed
benchmarks.population: Handovers of institutional and commercial buildings by a Canadian general contractor

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about four to eight weeks to certification and takeover, using the 20-day (CCDC 2-2008, src pawson) and 10-day (CCDC 2-2020, src mlt) consultant periods, then one to two months to close the consultant's list in the occupied building; winter handovers with seasonal items set the p90. No published measurement was found.

benchmarks.population: Ontario Construction Act from 1 July 2018 contracts

pain_points.description: Trades have moved crews to other projects and return slowly to fix deficiencies, especially after the owner has moved in.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from practice.

pain_points.description: Closeout documents (manuals, warranties, as-builts) arrive late and incomplete, holding up takeover and holdback.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from practice.

pain_points.description: Consultants and inspectors book walks and inspections one to two weeks out, and certification takes up to the full contract period.

evidence.note: Contract periods of 20 and 10 calendar days.

pain_points.description: Consultant deficiency lists arrive as PDFs or spreadsheets and are re-keyed into the platform, with duplicates and errors.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 practice.

sources.title: Stipulated Price Contract
sources.publisher: Canadian Consulting Engineer (Owen Pawson, Miller Thomson)
sources.supports: CCDC 2-2008: consultant reviews shop drawings with reasonable promptness so as to cause no delay (GC 3.10.12) and indicates acceptance or rejection of deviations in writing (GC 3.10.9); the contractor remains responsible for errors or omissions in shop drawings (GC 3.10.10); the consultant has 20 calendar days after the contractor submits an application and a list of items to be completed or corrected to verify substantial performance (GC 5.4.2); payment certificates within 10 calendar days (GC 5.3.1).

sources.title: The new CCDC 2 - 2020: contract changes you need to know
sources.supports: CCDC 2-2020 Ready-for-Takeover (GC 12.1) prerequisites include certified or verified substantial performance, evidence of occupancy compliance or an occupancy permit, final cleaning, operations and maintenance documentation, as-built drawings and start-up testing; the consultant has 10 calendar days to respond to the contractor's application; holdback is paid no later than 10 working days after the holdback period expires; substantial performance is as defined in the lien legislation of the place of the work.

sources.title: Prompt payment and adjudication have arrived in Ontario
sources.supports: Ontario Construction Act: prompt payment and adjudication in force 1 October 2019; holdback release mandatory unless the payer publishes a notice of non-payment of holdback; publication of a certificate of substantial performance is a trigger date; lien preservation period raised from 45 to 60 days and perfection to 90 days after the last day to preserve.

assumptions: The simulated median of about 114 days is above the 95-day tier C benchmark because 30% of back-checks send items back to the trades for another two-week round and winter handovers wait months for seasonal items; neither the benchmark nor the waits rest on a measured source.
A case runs from the superintendent's completion notice to closure of the consultant's deficiency list; warranty work after that is ops-warranty-service.
Turnover package assembly and training run in parallel with consultant certification in practice; the simulation adds their waits in sequence, so concurrent steps are given short waits.
Trade, consultant, inspector and owner time is outside the organisation and given zero touch time.

Statutory thresholds for substantial performance and the publication rules are those of the Ontario Construction Act; the statute itself could not be opened, so its rules are cited from law firm and contract summaries.
P3 handovers go to Project Co and the public sponsor, and building department occupancy inspections are an outside step; the organisation file lacks these two links.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (1.35 loading factor for salaried staff).

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24: the contractor sends the consultant an application for substantial performance; the consultant issues the certificate, so the output to consultant is now substantial_performance_application.
